edits.where: Discussion §6 ¶1 ("The comparison with five elite cultivars…"), whole paragraph
edits.why: Keep only what the Discussion adds to the Results: one haplotype per gene (expected in modern germplasm), why GH17 and PHT4;3 are uninformative (Morex is elite), and the conclusion. Deleted: sentence 1, which only announces what follows (this also settles item 6.6), and sentence 3, which restates Results Ch. 3 ¶8 and Ch. 4 ¶3. The per-gene detail (matched the low-fiber haplotypes; lacked the associated alleles) stays in the Results. The conclusion now names the two informative loci. About 147 → 85 words.
edits.old: The comparison with five elite cultivars showed which of the wild haplotypes are present in modern germplasm. The cultivars shared a single haplotype at each of the three genes carried forward from the haplotype analysis, as expected in modern germplasm. At the two genes where the comparison was informative, none of the cultivars carried the high-fiber haplotype: at the acyltransferase they matched the low-fiber wild haplotypes, and at the GDSL esterase/lipase they lacked the alleles of the associated SNPs that define it. At the glucanase and the phosphate transporter, by contrast, the cultivars carried the reference allele at every site, and since the reference genome, Morex, is itself an elite cultivar, these two genes are not informative for this comparison. Thus, the high-fiber haplotypes identified at two independent loci are absent from the elite lines examined, and may represent wild variation for increasing fiber in cultivated barley.
